subject.title: Telegram: apiRoot local Bot API server receives updates but never dispatches to agent sessions

question: Should Telegram local Bot API migration reset or scope update offsets by `apiRoot`, and should `deleteWebhook` tolerate the `400: Logged out` cooldown only for this migration path?
rationale: The source-backed failure path crosses persisted polling state and auth/startup error handling, so a fix changes upgrade behavior and could mask real Telegram client rejections if scoped too broadly.

options.title: Endpoint-scoped offset with narrow cooldown tolerance
options.body: Store or validate API-root identity for Telegram offsets, reset stale endpoint offsets through runtime or doctor, and tolerate only the known local Bot API migration `400: Logged out` cleanup case with live proof.

options.title: Document manual reset only
options.body: Keep runtime behavior unchanged and update docs/doctor diagnostics to tell operators how to reset local Bot API offsets and wait out the logOut cooldown manually.

options.title: Defer until live reproduction
options.body: Keep the issue open without implementation until a maintainer or reporter provides a live local Bot API transcript showing the raw-update-to-dispatch failure on current main.

recommendation.title: Endpoint-scoped offset with narrow cooldown tolerance
recommendation.body: Store or validate API-root identity for Telegram offsets, reset stale endpoint offsets through runtime or doctor, and tolerate only the known local Bot API migration `400: Logged out` cleanup case with live proof.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent current-main ownership and polling-session recovery work make this the best available routing candidate for the decision.
